referee:dfsb:proof.verdict: contains false statements. The core of Theorem thm:dfsb holds: soundness, the pilot constants, ratio propagation and the cost formula under its hypothesis. Verified correct:
(1) (F), (D)-and, (D)-or and (B) are exact identities under a product distribution. D(h)=D(h AND F)=D(F)D(h|_F) because h|_F is independent of F's variables.
(2) Pilot constants. Lower tail: the exponent (mu-t)^2/(2mu) increases in mu for mu>=t; at mu=N0/K it equals 18*ceil(ln(2m/delta)). Upper tail: e^{-mu}(e mu/t)^t increases for mu<t, giving (e/4)^{16 ceil(ln(2m/delta))} <= (delta/2m)^6. A union bound over at most 2m adaptively chosen pilots is fine. I also checked the bounds against exact binomial tails for K in {1,2,4,16,64}, m in {1,10,1000}, delta in {0.5,0.05,0.001}; all pass (chern.py).
(3) The pruning argument (actual tree is a pruning of T*_K, at most m nodes, leaves 16K-dense or envelope looseness at most 16K) is correct, given deterministic tie-breaking in (B).
(4) Ratio propagation:
- products multiply ratios;
- exact convex or scaled combinations do not increase them;
- for f(x)=1-prod(1-x_j), U<=bL implies f(U)<=b f(L). g(t)=f(tx) has g''=-e^h[(sum y_j)^2-sum y_j^2]<=0 on [0,1/max x_j]. When some b x_j>=1, f(x)>=x_j>=1/b directly. So 'concave along rays' needs only this domain caveat. Random trials (2e5) give max f(U)/(b f(L)) = 1+4e-16 (orratio.py).
(5) (1+eps/(3d))^d <= e^{eps/3} <= 1+eps for eps<=1. d<=n because leaves on one derivation have pairwise disjoint nonempty supports.
(6) The Phase-2 cost O~(l K d^2 eps^-2 log(l/delta)) follows from thm:envelope(iv) with looseness 16K and eta=eps/(3d). The example cost O(t^3 eps^-2 log(t/delta)) in (a) matches.
(7) Cor (c): any variable shared by two children after restriction and flattening is in Conf(C). Two flattened children reach the gate by paths that diverge at some gate with two distinct children both containing the variable. Every (B) variable is therefore in Conf, and fully assigned Conf makes every gate decomposable. The count O(s 3^r) holds; see the minor finding on the injectivity wording.
(8) R1-R7 each give phi >= 1_h with supp(phi_c) inside sv(c), so Prod gates stay decomposable.
(9) prop:dnnf-env: the DNNF's own circuit has support C^{-1}(1), so K=E[phi|C=1], and K<=m for a DNF.
(10) thm:meta: the union bound and the claim that the intersection of intervals is no looser than its tightest member are correct.
(11) The distributed-surprise arithmetic (at most n/3 disjoint 3-clauses, K>=(8/7)^{m-n/3}) is correct up to the expectation issue noted below.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:part1-limits, sentence 'so no general procedure beats sampling by more than a factor 2^{o(log(1/p))} on the satisfiable ones' (and the preceding 'under the exponential-time hypothesis')
findings.problem: The conclusion does not follow from ETH and is false. ETH only says 3-SAT needs time 2^{cn} for some unspecified c>0. That bounds the cost from below by p^{-c}, not by p^{-1+o(1)}. Known algorithms refute the claim outright: plain clause branching (x1=1 | x1=0,x2=1 | x1=0,x2=0,x3=1) counts 3-SAT models exactly in O*(1.8393^n), and published #3SAT algorithms reach about 1.64^n. That is a sound procedure, complete on all 3-CNFs. On a uniquely satisfiable 3-CNF (p=2^{-n}) Monte Carlo costs about 2^n eps^-2 log(1/delta), so the speed-up is (2/1.8393)^n = p^{-0.12}, which is 2^{Theta(log 1/p)}, not 2^{o(log 1/p)}. Separately, the procedures are randomized, so the hypothesis needed is randomized ETH, not ETH as defined by Impagliazzo-Paturi.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'Under randomized ETH, no sound procedure that is complete on satisfiable 3-CNFs runs in time 2^{o(n)}poly(|C|). In particular none has cost 2^{o(log(1/p))}poly(|C|), i.e. subexponential in the surprise. (Run it with a time cut-off and answer SAT iff L>0.)' If an 'at most a 2^{o(n)} speed-up' statement is wanted, it needs randomized SETH and CNFs of unbounded width. Even then it bounds the speed-up by 2^{o(n)}, not by 2^{o(log 1/p)}.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Corollary cor:dfsb(a), 'This includes ... read-once compositions F(lambda_1,...,lambda_t) of arbitrary K-dense circuits'; also (b) 'm_K(C)=O(1)' and the AND-of-blocks example
findings.problem: The rules run in the order T,F,D,S,E,B, so (D) is applied before the density test (S). A K-dense lambda_i whose top gate is a decomposable OR gets split, and its component-tree leaves can be arbitrarily rare. Then the hypothesis of (a) fails and m_K is not O(s). Counterexample: C = y OR mu (t=1, F = identity, lambda = y OR mu is 1/2-dense), with mu a rare non-decomposable circuit. The component tree has leaf mu with D(mu) tiny, and T*_K contains the whole branching tree of mu. Measured with the repository's DFSB (K=4, envelopes off), mu = planted system of k/2 XOR equations of weight k/2: 225 nodes at k=12 (48 wires), 1537 at k=16 (78 wires), and over 3000 at k=20 (117 wires), about 2^{0.7k}. With mu a PRG-preimage circuit, a polynomial m_K(mu) would contradict prop:worstcase(b). The same issue breaks (b): if C|_F is (D)-decomposable, the tree is not O(1). With j AND-parts the cost picks up d=j. With OR-parts it can be exponential.
findings.fix: Either (i) restrict the claim: '...of K-dense circuits lambda_i whose own component trees have all leaves of probability >= 1/K (e.g. lambda_i not decomposable after forcing)', and in (b) assume C|_F is not (D)-decomposable. Or (ii) change the algorithm: apply (S) before (D) at OR nodes, with (D)-AND still first, and re-prove (a). Option (ii) keeps exactness for read-once formulas only if (S) is skipped at nodes all of whose children are exactly computable.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:dfsb Phase 1/Phase 2 description and Theorem thm:dfsb (cost); used by Theorem thm:meta ('runs in polynomial time')
findings.problem: Phase 2 is said to estimate 'every leaf' to relative accuracy eps/(3d), but nothing is specified for the 'loose' leaves created when the node budget is exceeded. It also puts no cap on the sequential stopping rule. A loose leaf, or a leaf wrongly accepted on the pilot-failure event, can have density about p, so Phase 2 runs for about 1/p samples. As written, DFSB is therefore not 'efficient' in the sense of Def. def:sound on every circuit, and thm:meta's polynomial-time claim does not follow. The code does cap (max_leaf_samples, and 10^5 for loose leaves), but the paper does not say so. Separately, for envelope leaves with boxes (R7), Phase 2 re-estimates the box masses. The pilot's acceptance therefore does not certify looseness at most 16K for the proposal actually used.
findings.fix: Add to the algorithm: each leaf runs the doubling stopping rule of thm:envelope(iv) up to a cap N_max = c*16K*(3d/eps)^2*(log(l/delta)+loglog K). If it has not stopped by then, it outputs its current KL interval, which is valid because the stage-wise intervals are simultaneously valid. Loose leaves get a KL interval from N_max Monte Carlo samples, or [0,1]. Then state the total running time as polynomial on every circuit. For box envelopes, either reuse the pilot's box estimates in Phase 2 or include the box-estimation error in the looseness bound (rho_max/rho_min).

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, rule (R8) 'replaced, before anything else, ... This makes every class above closed under local rewriting' versus Cor. cor:dfsb(a) 'read-once formulas (exactly)' and (c)
findings.problem: The scope of R8 is ambiguous: it is listed as an envelope rule but is said to apply 'before anything else' to make the DFSB classes closed. If it rewrites the circuit DFSB works on, it conflicts with the corollary. The reduced OBDD's NNF ((NOT v AND f0) OR (v AND f1), with f0 and f1 sharing variables and sub-diagrams) is non-decomposable, so DFSB turns such nodes into Monte Carlo leaves or branches on them. The OBDD variables also enter Conf(C). Measured with the repository code (small_cone=10, i.e. R8): the read-once formula AND_{j<=8}((a_j AND b_j) OR (c_j AND d_j)) gives 8 MC leaves and the interval [0.951, 1.035]*p, not an exact value. With R8 off it is exact. The blanket closure claim is also unproved and false for rewrites whose gadgets touch large-support sub-circuits. For example, A AND B -> (A AND B) AND (A OR B) destroys decomposability, and R8 cannot repair it.
findings.fix: Make R8-OBDDs atomic: add to (T) 'h is an OBDD produced by (R8): exact value by one bottom-up pass'. Compute Conf(C) and the component tree with these gates as leaves. Then (a) and (c) survive with s counting the rewritten circuit. Restrict the closure claim to 'rewritings confined to cones of at most c log|C| variables'.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:modules, item 'Algebraic. Affine and degree-2 constraints over F_2 ... exact counting and sampling by Gaussian elimination and Dickson's normal form [ek1990]'
findings.problem: For a conjunction of several quadratic equations over F_2, even satisfiability is NP-complete (the MQ problem), and counting is #P-hard. Ehrenfeucht-Karpinski gives polynomial-time counting for a single degree-2 polynomial; affine constraints can be substituted into it. Read literally as 'systems of affine and degree-2 constraints', the module would make thm:meta complete on an NP-hard class. That contradicts prop:worstcase(a) unless NP is in BPP.
findings.fix: State: 'an affine system together with at most one quadratic equation (equivalently, one quadratic form restricted to an affine subspace) under the uniform distribution: exact counting and sampling by Gaussian elimination and Dickson's normal form; products of such pieces on disjoint supports are usable as envelope pieces.'

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Corollary cor:dfsb(c) 'with K=1 DFSB is exact cutset conditioning: no sampling at all' and its proof 'two distinct tree nodes cannot carry the same NNF node and the same partial assignment'
findings.problem: (1) With K=1 the actual pilot accepts every node of density at least 1/(16K)=1/16. For example, (x OR y) AND (x OR z) has density 5/8 and can become an MC leaf. Even the ideal predicate D(h)>=1 turns non-literal tautological nodes into MC leaves. So DFSB with K=1 does sample. (2) Injectivity fails literally: an (F) node and its child h|_F carry the same original gate with the same Conf-assignment when F has no Conf variables. The map is at most 2-to-1 (unit propagation is idempotent), so O(s 3^r) still holds.
findings.fix: Say 'DFSB with (S) and (E) disabled is exact cutset conditioning', or let (S) accept only nodes with D(h)=1 recognised syntactically. In the proof, map tree nodes to (gate or child-group, Conf-assignment, flag for force-wrapper) and note that the map is at most 2-to-1.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Theorem thm:dfsb cost '... each costing O(|C|); the non-sampling work is O(m|C|)'; sec-setting.tex 'with at most two copies of every gate'
findings.problem: Several costs are not counted. Envelope leaves cost O(|C|+|Phi|) per sample, and |Phi| can be 2^r|C| after R4 Shannon expansions. Box envelopes cost O(LR max|B_j|) in expectation, plus box estimation. Building Phi_h at every node reaching (E) is extra non-sampling work. So is R8 tabulation (about |C|^{c+1}), as are failed-literal probing (O(n|C|) or more) and Gaussian elimination at the root. Also, the NNF of a circuit with XOR or threshold gates is not a two-copies-per-gate {AND,OR}-circuit. A fan-in-k XOR needs O(k) gates per polarity, and weighted thresholds need a DP over partial sums: pseudo-polynomial, or no small NNF at all (the code uses opaque nodes). DFSB, Conf(C) and the O(|C|) bounds all depend on this.
findings.fix: State per-sample cost as O(|C|+|Phi_h|) (plus box costs). State non-sampling work as O(m(|C|+max_h|Phi_h|)) + O(|C|^{c+1}) + root preprocessing. In sec:setting, say the NNF has size O(|C|) for AND/OR/NOT/XOR circuits, and that threshold gates are expanded by a sum DP or treated as opaque leaves.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sentence after thm:dfsb 'The class on which DFSB beats sampling is therefore {C: m_K(C) <= poly(|C|) for some K <= poly(|C|)}' and sec:part1 intro 'characterised by the size of a canonical explanation tree'
findings.problem: thm:dfsb gives only a sufficient condition. DFSB is tight on circuits with superpolynomial m_K, e.g. y OR mu above, where loose leaves under a rare OR-branch do not matter: at k=20 the output was [0.50036, 0.50075] with the budget exhausted. findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Theorem thm:meta and its proof
findings.problem: (1) M is undefined. (2) If the intersection is empty (some interval invalid, probability at most delta), the output is unspecified. (3) DFSB's parameters K and m must be fixed polynomials for 'polynomial time' and for completeness on a fixed class. (4) The completeness probability is 1-delta/M-delta, not 1-delta. referee:ctx-modules:proof.verdict: contains false statements. The construction and proof of Theorem thm:cw and the proof of Lemma lem:quotient are correct. The problem is the definition of context width: it says nested gates are flattened, and under that definition the Example's claim cw=O(w) is false, the NNF is not of size at most 2|C|, and the parameter no longer generalises dtrees. The implementation and experiments use the unflattened NNF. There are also some smaller missing hypotheses, and one empirical claim nothing supports. All of these are fixable in place.
referee:ctx-modules:proof.checked:
Re-derived every step of thm:cw.
- F1 holds: Up(h) contains Up(g), so kappa(g) ∩ sv(h) is contained in kappa(h).
- F2 holds, because S_g is contained in sv(g) and g is in Up(g).
- M-nodes are deterministic Shannon expansions, and pi ∪ tau covers kappa(h) by F1.
- Correctness follows by induction from g|σ = op_j h_j|σ.
- Decomposability holds. M[h,pi] mentions only sv(h) \ dom(pi), and N[h,σ] mentions only sv(h) \ kappa(h), so the children of an ∧ are on the sets sv(h_j) \ kappa(g), which F2 makes pairwise disjoint.
- Size: each wire adds at most 2^|kappa(h)| ∧-terms of at most cw+1 wires each.
- cw=0 iff DNNF, since S_g is contained in kappa(g).
- The d-DNNF claim holds: conditioning preserves disjointness.
- The FPRAS corollary follows: smoothing and comparators give #E' = (∏ b_i) D(E), then the #DNNF FPRAS applies.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Definition [context width] ('Work in the NNF of C (size ≤2|C|, nested gates flattened)') together with Example [∨'s are easy, ∧'s are hard] ('Then cw=O(w)') and the claim that cw 'generalises Darwiche's dtree conditioning'
findings.problem:
Flattening merges a CNF's ∧-tree into a single ∧-gate. Its overlap S_g is then every variable that occurs in two clauses, so kappa(top) is almost all variables. For window CNFs the flattened definition gives cw = n−2, not O(w).

Measured with the project code:
- or_of_chain_cnfs(n,4,3) has cw 11/31/51 for n = 20/40/60 when flattened, against 3 unflattened.
- A single window CNF with n = 30/60 has cw 28/58 when flattened or written as a flat ∧. A left-deep chain in window order gives 3; a shuffled chain gives 27/47.

So the Example is false under the paper's own definition. The definition also contradicts:
- the implementation (exp_ctx.py, meta.py and the tests all call to_nnf(C, flatten=False), and the families.py docstring says the left-deep chain 'is what makes the context width small');
- sec-experiments, which says 'built as left-deep ∧-chains';
- the dtree analogy, since a flattened CNF has no dtree.

More generally, cw is not an invariant of the function. It depends on how the ∧'s are bracketed.
findings.fix:
Delete 'nested gates flattened'.

Define cw(N) for a given NNF N in which each ∧-gate is bracketed as given; a binary ∧-tree over a gate's children is a dtree. Optionally define cw(C) as the minimum over bracketings and note that any bracketing the algorithm chooses gives an upper bound.

Restate the Example: 'if each F_i is written as a left-deep ∧-chain of its clauses in window order, then kappa(chain prefix) has w−1 variables and kappa(clause) has w, so cw = w'.

For the intro's 'ORs of bounded-pathwidth CNFs', say that the bracketing comes from a path decomposition. That is computable in linear time for constant width (Bodlaender–Kloks), or it must be given.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Definition [context width] 'size ≤2|C|' and Theorem thm:cw 'Every circuit C is equivalent to a DNNF of size O(|C| cw 2^cw)'
findings.problem:
An NNF of size at most 2|C| exists only for {∧,∨,¬}-circuits without flattening. The paper's gate basis (sec-setting) also has ⊕ and weighted thresholds.
- ⊕: a 6-input XOR has 6 wires but 54 NNF wires (measured).
- Weighted thresholds: no linear-size NNF is given. The code turns large-weight THR gates into opaque nodes, and compile_ctx then returns None.
- Flattening: it can square the size. An OR of the prefixes of an ∧-chain goes from 237 to 3,318 wires.

So a size bound in |C| 'for every circuit' does not follow.
findings.fix:
State the theorem for an NNF N of C: 'C is equivalent to a DNNF of size O(|N|(cw(N)+1)2^{cw(N)})'.

Add that |N| = O(|C|) for {∧,∨,¬,⊕}-circuits, where a fan-in-k ⊕ costs O(k) gates per polarity. A threshold gate with nonnegative integer weights of total W costs O(kW) by the sequential-counter DP. Other threshold gates must be frontier gates (see the frontier remark), or the class must be restricted.

findings.location: Paper text: sec-part1.tex, sec:modules-quotients, paragraph after Lemma lem:quotient: 'a threshold of 80 random modules with p≈10^{-15} is estimated to 0.1% in seconds'
findings.problem:
Nothing in the repository supports this quantitative claim:
- code/rareprob has no module detection, module tree or quotient estimator (grep finds no module, quotient or dominator code in code/ or experiments/);
- no experiment script or results file reports it.

The closest experiment is the 'threshold' family in speedup.json. It uses exponential tilting, not modules, and reports interval ratios of about 1.08 (8%) at p≈2.5e-15 with 400 blocks, not 0.1%.
findings.fix: Either remove the sentence, or add the experiment and its results file and name the method. If modules are tabulated exactly and the threshold DP is exact, the answer is exact, and the text should say so rather than '0.1%'.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Lemma lem:quotient, the monotone/antitone clause
findings.problem:
The one-sided monotone case silently assumes q̂ ∈ [0,1]^k. Without that, the A and B at intermediate points of the coordinate-by-coordinate argument can be negative, so A ≥ B fails.

Counterexample: Q = y1 ∧ (y2 ∨ y3), q = (0.870, 0.772, 0.830), q̂ = q·e^ξ = (2.46, 2.49, 3.34). Then F(q̂) = −6.11 while F(q) = 0.84.

In the two-sided case q̂ ∈ (0,1) follows automatically. With that hypothesis the proof is correct; I checked it algebraically and numerically.
findings.fix: Add 'with q̂ ∈ [0,1]^k' to the lemma. Note that clipping an estimate to [0,1] keeps the one-sided condition true, because the true q_j lies between the clipped and unclipped values.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, paragraph after Lemma lem:quotient: 'gives a sound estimator whose relative error is the sum of the modules' errors'
findings.problem:
Three things are missing.
- For coordinates where the quotient is neither monotone nor antitone (e.g. ⊕ of modules), the lemma needs relative accuracy on 1−q_j. A sound interval [L_j, U_j] for q_j gives 1−q_j only to relative error (U_j−L_j)/(1−U_j), which is useless when q_j ≈ 1.
- Confidence must be split across modules.
- When the quotient is estimated by DFSB or Monte Carlo under ⊗Bern(q̂), that interval is for F(q̂) and has to be moved to F(q) through the lemma.
findings.fix:
Spell out the composition rule.
- Given q_j ∈ [L_j, U_j], take any q̂_j in that interval and set ξ_j = max(log(U_j/L_j), log((1−L_j)/(1−U_j))). Monotone or antitone coordinates need only the relevant term. Then F(q) ∈ e^{±Σξ_j}·F(q̂).
- When the complement term is large, also estimate ¬g.
- Run each module and each quotient estimate at confidence δ/(number of estimates), and take a union bound.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Theorem thm:cw size/time bound and proof sentence 'Each wire contributes O(cw 2^cw) nodes'
findings.problem: O(|C|·cw·2^cw) is zero when cw = 0. Each wire actually adds at most 2^|kappa(h)| nodes and O((cw+1)2^cw) wires. 'Computable in the same time' leaves out the O(|N|·n) bit operations needed to compute supports, overlaps and contexts, which dominates when n is much larger than cw·2^cw.
findings.fix: Write: size O(|N|(cw+1)2^cw), computable in time O(|N|(n/wordsize + (cw+1)2^cw)). Numerically, output wires stay at most |N|(cw+1)2^cw on 600 random circuits.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Theorem thm:cw 'If moreover every ∨-gate has semantically disjoint children, the result is a d-DNNF'
findings.problem: It is unclear whose ∨-gates are meant. The hypothesis has to hold for every ∨-gate of the NNF in the root's cone. That includes ∨'s created by De Morgan from ∧'s under a negation, and those from ⊕ or threshold expansions. Example: C = ¬(a ∧ b) has no ∨-gate, but its NNF ¬a ∨ ¬b is not deterministic. The proof itself is correct; I tested it on 530 NNFs with deterministic ∨'s, and phi only takes the values 0 and 1.
findings.fix: Write 'if every ∨-gate of the NNF N is deterministic (h_i ∧ h_j ≡ 0)'. Optionally add the consequence: p is then computable exactly in time O(|N|(cw+1)2^cw) under any product distribution.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Example: 'so an FPRAS exists' and 'counting vertex covers in graphs of degree ≥3 is #P-complete'
findings.problem:
Two problems with the wording.
- The FPRAS time is poly(|C|·2^w), so it is polynomial only when w = O(log n).
- 'Degree ≥3' literally means minimum degree, which does not give a bounded Δ, and the claim has no citation.

The inclusion–exclusion reduction itself is correct. It is a Turing reduction with 2^{Δ+1}−1 oracle calls, and I verified it numerically on 30 random graphs of maximum degree 3. Any proper edge colouring with O(Δ) colours works (Vizing/Misra–Gries gives Δ+1).
findings.fix: Write: 'Then cw = w (for the chain bracketing), so an FPRAS exists when w = O(log n)'. Write also: 'counting vertex covers (equivalently independent sets) is #P-complete already in graphs of maximum degree 3 [Greenhill 2000, Comput. Complexity 9:52–72]'.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:ctxwidth, frontier remark: 'bounded treewidth by \cite{darwiche2009}'
findings.problem: darwiche2009 is a Bayesian-network textbook (CNF/jointree compilation). Compiling a circuit gate of bounded treewidth that way goes through a Tseitin CNF, and the gate variables then have to be projected out. Projection keeps the DNNF property but can destroy determinism, so the d-DNNF clause of thm:cw does not carry over to such frontiers. The size bound also has to include the frontier compilations, each multiplied by 2^|kappa(f)|.
findings.fix:
Cite Amarilli–Capelli–Monet–Senellart, 'Connecting knowledge compilation classes and width parameters' (Theory Comput. Syst. 2020), which gives d-SDNNFs of size 2^{O(k)}|C| for treewidth-k circuits.

Add: the size becomes Σ_f 2^{|kappa(f)|}·|DNNF(f)| plus the bound for the remaining gates. The result is a d-DNNF only if the frontier compilations are deterministic.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:modules-quotients: 'Modules form a laminar family and can be found in O(|C| n) time with dominators, as in fault-tree analysis \cite{dutuitrauzy1996}'
findings.problem:
The statements are true: I checked laminarity and the factorisation C = Q_g(g, x_rest) by brute force on 792 modules in 300 random circuits, with no violations.

Two things should change.
- 'Laminar family' should say of what: the supports, and hence the cones.
- To my knowledge, Dutuit–Rauzy give a linear-time algorithm based on DFS visit dates, not dominators, so the citation does not back the stated method, and the O(|C|n) bound is weaker than the cited result.
findings.fix:
Add the one-line proof: if v ∈ sv(g) ∩ sv(h), every path from x_v to the output passes through both g and h, so one is in the other's cone and the supports are nested.

Then write either 'found in linear time [DR96]' or 'in O(|C|n) time: g is a module iff every input of sv(g) lies in g's subtree of the post-dominator tree of C (dominator tree of the reversed DAG rooted at the output)'.

referee:dfsb:counterexample.verdict: contains false statements. Theorem thm:dfsb (soundness, the pilot thresholds, the pruning argument, the interval-ratio propagation) is correct. Several claims around it are false as written: the "read-once compositions" inclusion in cor:dfsb(a), the O(1) tree size and cost in cor:dfsb(b), "no sampling at all" with K=1 in cor:dfsb(c), "read-once formulas (exactly)" once (R8) is applied, and the speed-up bound drawn from ETH in sec:part1-limits. Each has a short fix, given below.
referee:dfsb:counterexample.checked:
Read sec-part1.tex in full, plus sec-setting, sec-envelopes and sec-limits (for prop:worstcase), thm:sis in sec-part2, the appendix, and the refs.bib entries cited in my sections. Read code/rareprob/dfsb.py, nnf.py, cnf.py, compile.py and envelope.py to fix the rule order and the (R8) behaviour. All scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-AI-works/02f29707-9759-5ff3-9757-46e1f8b0fdfe/scratchpad.

Checked and correct:
(1) (T), (F), (D) and (B) are exact identities under product D. Phase-2 validity follows by a union bound conditional on the Phase-1 tree. All node operations are monotone.
(2) The pilot tail bounds. Exact binomial tails, for K in {1,2,4,64,1000}, m in {1,10,1000} and delta in {0.5,0.05,1e-6}, never exceed (delta/2m)^18 for density >= 1/K or (delta/2m)^6 for density < 1/(16K) (exp1_pilot.py).
(3) The (D)-OR ratio lemma: f(x') <= b f(x) for x' <= bx in [0,1]^k with b >= 1, and f(x') >= a f(x) for x' >= ax. I proved it by induction on k and checked 20000 random instances in exact rational arithmetic (exp1b.py). A float version shows spurious violations up to 1.11 from cancellation in 1-prod(1-x), so implementations need log1p/expm1, which dfsb._combine already uses.
(4) (1+eps/(3d))^d <= e^{eps/3} <= 1+eps holds for eps <= 1.
(5) Pruning: on the good pilot event the actual tree is a pruning of T*_K. It also contains T*_{16K} as a pruning when (E) is off, so |T*_{16K}| <= |actual tree| <= |T*_K|.
(6) cor(c)'s O(s 3^r) bound. I built an exact ideal-tree builder (ideal.py: the repo's DFSB with exact densities and no (E)) and ran it on 300 random formulas with |Conf| <= 5 and random product D, including q near 0 and 1. Nodes never exceeded s*3^r, and when every leaf was exact the combined value matched exact_prob (exp6_cutset.py).
(7) Soundness of the full DFSB on random small circuits with repeated children, XOR and NOT, and some q_i in {0,1}, at delta=0.1: 398 misses in 110842 runs. That is consistent with soundness. One crash appeared (see findings) (exp8_sound.py, exp9b.py).
(8) Citations I could check offline (Pearl 1988, Impagliazzo-Paturi 2001, Bodlaender et al. 2016, Ehrenfeucht-Karpinski 1990, Gopalan-Klivans-Meka 2010) match their use. I could not check the 2^{k/4.82} constant attributed to wangyin2024, because this run's web-search budget was used up.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, cor:dfsb(a): "This includes read-once formulas (exactly) and read-once compositions F(lambda_1,...,lambda_t) of arbitrary K-dense circuits on disjoint variable sets"
findings.problem:
The inclusion claim is false, for two separate reasons.
(i) Negation. Read-once F may negate an input. Take F(y) = NOT y and lambda = NOT C. Then lambda is K-dense for any circuit C with p <= 1-1/K, and F(lambda) = C. The claim would then give m_K(C) = O(s) for every such C, so DFSB would be complete on all 3-CNFs. By prop:worstcase(a) that implies NP is contained in BPP.
(ii) Rule order, even for monotone F. (D) is tried before (S), in the paper's list and in dfsb.py build(). So a dense lambda that is an OR of variable-disjoint rare parts gets split, and the rare parts must be branched. Example: lambda = OR over i <= t of a_i, where a_i is a cycle CNF on L fresh variables, q = 1/2, and t ~ 1/D(a_i), so D(lambda) ~ 0.64 >= 1/K with K = 4. Exact ideal trees for L = 12, 14, 16, 18 give |C| = 170, 286, 511, 856 and m_K = 209, 590, 1651, 4366. The ratio m_K/|C| = 1.23, 2.06, 3.23, 5.10 keeps growing, so m_K is not O(s) (exp5_or.py).
findings.fix: Restrict the example to monotone F, or require each lambda_i to be K-dense in the polarity in which it occurs. Also require each lambda_i to satisfy the hypothesis of (a) itself, i.e. be force-free and non-decomposable, or have K-dense component-tree leaves. Alternatively, test (S) before splitting at (D)-OR nodes; then re-check the exactness claim for read-once formulas under that order.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, cor:dfsb(b): "then m_K(C)=O(1) and the cost is O(K eps^-2 log(1/delta))"
findings.problem: This is false whenever C|_F is decomposable, because (D) precedes (S). Counterexample: C = [x_A = 1^20] AND (AND over i <= t of B_i), where B_i is an OR of r = ceil(log2 t)+1 disjoint maj3 gates. D(C|F) ~ 0.60 >= 1/K with K = 4. The exact ideal tree T*_4 has m_K = 41, 97, 225, 513 for t = 8, 16, 32, 64, with 32 to 448 MC leaves and d = t (exp4b.py). Phase-2 cost grows like l*K*d^2/eps^2, roughly t^3 log t, not O(K eps^-2 log(1/delta)).
findings.fix: State m_K(C) = 1 + m_K(C|_F), with the cost given by thm:dfsb applied to that tree. The O(1) claim holds only if C|_F is not decomposable, or if (S) is tested on the (F)-child before (D).

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, cor:dfsb(c): "with K=1 DFSB is exact cutset conditioning: no sampling at all"; proof: "two distinct tree nodes cannot carry the same NNF node and the same partial assignment"
findings.problem:
(i) DFSB with K=1 still samples. It runs a pilot of N_0 = 64*ceil(ln(2m/delta)) samples at every non-decomposable node, and the completeness analysis allows it to accept any node of density >= 1/16 as an MC leaf. Repo run: an AND of 8 multiplexers (x_i ? y_i : z_i), so Conf = {x_1..x_8} and r = 8, gives 8 MC leaves and the interval [0.00384, 0.00409] around p = 2^-8. It is not exact (exp3b_mux.py).
(ii) Even the ideal tree T*_1 accepts non-syntactic tautologies (D(h) = 1) as (S)-leaves, e.g. (x AND y) OR NOT x OR NOT y. Three of 300 random small-Conf formulas had such leaves.
(iii) The injectivity sentence is false as written: an (F) wrapper and its child carry the same NNF gate and the same Conf-assignment, and so can several virtual child-group nodes. The O(s 3^r) bound itself holds; numerically nodes <= s*3^r in all 300 trials.
findings.fix: Say: 'with (S) and (E) disabled (never accept), DFSB is exact cutset conditioning with O(s 3^r) nodes; pilots then cost nothing'. Replace the injectivity claim with: 'each pair (gate g, Conf-assignment) is carried by at most O(fan-in(g)+1) tree nodes (g, its (F)-child, and child groups of g)', which still gives O(s 3^r) since s counts wires.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, (R8) "replaced, before anything else, by its exact reduced OBDD ... This makes every class above closed under local rewriting"; interaction with cor:dfsb(a) "read-once formulas (exactly)" and Conf in (c)
findings.problem:
(R8) turns each small-support gate into an OBDD-NNF of the form (x AND f1) OR (NOT x AND f0). The two OR children share x, so (D) no longer applies at these gates and Conf(C) grows.
Repo run: the read-once formula AND over i <= 30 of (x_i OR y_i), with (R8) as implemented in nnf.to_nnf, gives a tree of 30 MC leaves and the interval [1.64e-4, 1.95e-4] around p = 1.786e-4, at both K=1 and K=4. It is not exact (exp3_readonce.py).
The closure claim is also unproved, and it fails for local rewrites at large-support gates. Absorption C' = AND(B_1..B_t, OR(AND_i B_i, y)) equals C = AND_i B_i and adds O(1) gates. But it puts every variable in Conf and makes the root non-decomposable, so without (E) the ideal tree must branch through the B_i, giving an exponential m_K.
findings.fix: Treat an (R8)-canonicalised gate as an exact leaf (T'): its probability is read off the OBDD in linear time, and its internal nodes are hidden from (D), (B) and Conf. Restrict the closure claim to rewrites confined to cones of support <= c log|C|, and state it for the procedure with (T').

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:part1-limits: "under the exponential-time hypothesis ... so no general procedure beats sampling by more than a factor 2^{o(log(1/p))} on the satisfiable ones"
findings.problem: The conclusion does not follow from ETH, and in its natural reading it is false. ETH gives only a 2^{cn} lower bound for some unspecified c > 0. Exact #3-SAT by branching on an unsatisfied clause (T(n) = T(n-1)+T(n-2)+T(n-3)) runs in O*(1.8393^n). On 3-CNFs with a unique solution (p = 2^-n), where sampling costs about 2^n/eps^2, this is a speed-up of 2^{0.12 log(1/p)}. That is not 2^{o(log 1/p)}. Also, the procedures are randomized, so randomized ETH is needed. The parallel conclusion in sec:limits for PRGs is correct only because there T(k) = 2^{(1-o(1))k}.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'under randomized ETH, no sound procedure complete on all 3-CNFs runs in time 2^{o(log(1/p))}*poly(|C|) on satisfiable instances. Otherwise, with a time-out, it would decide 3-SAT in 2^{o(n)}. So the cost must be (1/p)^{Omega(1)} on some instances.' Drop the 'beats sampling by at most 2^{o(log 1/p)}' phrasing.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:part1-limits, distributed surprise: "p <= (7/8)^m", "1/3 < alpha < alpha_sat", "except where exact Las Vegas samplers exist (thm:cftp, for unate circuits)"
findings.problem:
(i) p <= (7/8)^m is not a per-instance fact; only E[p] = (7/8)^m holds. With n = 20, alpha in {1, 2, 3} and 100 random instances each, 42-48% of instances have p > (7/8)^m, with a maximum ratio of 4.2 (exp7_3cnf.py).
(ii) For k = 3, a constant threshold alpha_sat is not known to exist; Friedgut's sharp threshold is non-uniform.
(iii) Exact Las Vegas samplers are not limited to unate circuits: partial rejection sampling (Guo-Jerrum-Liu) is exact for general CNFs, though fast only in restricted regimes. 'No polynomial-time test certifies' is an assertion, not a result.
findings.fix: Write: by Markov, with probability >= 1-1/n, p <= n(7/8)^m, so K >= (8/7)^{m-n/3}/n w.h.p. Replace alpha_sat with 'alpha below the (non-uniform) satisfiability threshold', or a proven range. Soften the certification sentence and mention partial rejection sampling.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:part1-limits, pseudorandom rarity: "Preimages [G(x)=y] of hash functions or PRGs ... nothing beats sampling by more than a subexponential factor unless the primitive is broken"
findings.problem: prop:worstcase(b) covers only length-doubling PRGs. It gives 'at most subexponential speed-up' only when the security is T(k) = 2^{(1-o(1))k} against advantage-1/2 distinguishers. A PRG with 2^{k/2} security is not 'broken', yet it leaves room for a 2^{k/2} speed-up. Hash-function preimages (compressing H) are not covered by (b) at all.
findings.fix: Say 'unless G has less than 2^{(1-o(1))k} security', and either drop hash functions or prove the analogous statement for them.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, thm:dfsb: "the non-sampling work is O(m*|C|)" and "each costing O(|C|)"
findings.problem: This omits several costs. Root failed-literal probing is O(n|C|) per round (dfsb/cnf code runs 3 rounds). Gaussian elimination is O(n^3). (R8) tabulation needs |C|^c evaluations for each small-support gate, up to |C|^{c+2} work in total. Envelope construction for (E), with Shannon expansions per (R4), costs up to 2^r|C| per node. Each (E) pilot or Phase-2 sample costs O(|C|+|Phi|), not O(|C|).
findings.fix: List these terms, e.g. O(m|C| + n^2|C| + n^3 + |C|^{c+2} + m*|Phi_max|), and charge envelope samples O(|C|+|Phi|).

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, thm:dfsb statement and "The class on which DFSB beats sampling is therefore {C: m_K(C) <= poly(|C|) for some K <= poly(|C|)}"
findings.problem: (i) K and m are inputs of the procedure. Completeness on this class needs a search over (K, m), and caps on Phase-2 samples for loose or wrongly accepted leaves; otherwise the procedure is not 'efficient' on all inputs in the sense of Def. def:sound. (ii) 'Therefore' overstates: the condition is sufficient only, since (E) leaves enlarge the class. (iii) With (R7) boxes, the (E) pilot measures E_{Q-hat}[W], which is distorted by rho in [rho_min, rho_max], so 'looseness at most 16K' holds only up to that factor.
findings.fix: Add a doubling search: K = m = 2^j with delta_j = delta/(2j^2), stop at the first tight output and intersect the intervals; add explicit per-leaf sample caps. State the two-sided characterisation |T*_{16K}| <= |tree| <= |T*_K| (without (E)). Include the rho distortion in the (E) acceptance analysis.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, rule (F) and (R2); thm:envelope / rule (E) when Z = 0
findings.problem: Edge cases are undefined. If unit propagation reaches a conflict, F contains complementary literals: D(F) read as a product of marginals is positive, and (R2)'s product [x][NOT x] is not decomposable. An envelope with mass Z = 0, possible when some q_i is 0 or 1, has no Q_phi. The implementation crashes on this case: dfsb._pilot_env -> envelope.py:242 'assert m[self.root] > 0', reproduced on a 3-variable circuit with q = (0, 0.306, 1) and p = 0 (exp9b.py).
findings.fix: Add: 'if propagation refutes h, D(h) = 0 (phi = 0)'; and 'if Z_Phi = 0 then D(h) = 0 exactly (phi >= 1_h), so h is an exact zero leaf'. In code, return a const-0 leaf when the envelope mass is 0.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, prop:dnnf-env
findings.problem: (i) If (R6) is active ('used whenever the rules give mass > 1'), sub-envelopes can be replaced by 1, so K <= E[phi | C=1], not equality. (ii) A DNF's NNF is a DNNF only if no term contains x and NOT x or a repeated literal. (iii) The FPRAS route via thm:sis needs rational marginals, with time polynomial in their bit size; the proposition states no such restriction. (iv) (R7) boxes are not DNNF leaves, so '(R1)-(R8) turn into a DNNF envelope' should exclude (R7).
findings.fix: State K <= E_D[phi | C=1], with equality when only (R1)-(R3) are used. Require consistent, duplicate-free terms. Add 'product D with rational marginals'. Write '(R1)-(R6), (R8)'.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:modules: "Algebraic. Affine and degree-2 constraints over F_2 ... exact counting ... by Gaussian elimination and Dickson's normal form"
findings.problem: Systems of several quadratic equations over F_2 are NP-hard even to decide (MQ). Exact counting is polynomial only for an affine system plus O(log n) quadratic constraints: substitute the affine part, then use #{f_1 = ... = f_c = 0} = 2^-c * sum over S of sum over x of (-1)^{sum_{i in S} f_i}, with each sum evaluated via Dickson.
findings.fix: Say 'affine constraints together with O(log n) degree-2 constraints'.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:modules, bounded-treewidth and local-lemma bullets
findings.problem: (i) 'Along a greedy elimination order' gives no width guarantee, so completeness on bounded-treewidth circuits needs the Bodlaender et al. decomposition that the text cites but does not use. (ii) d <= 2^{ck} is the LLL condition for the uniform distribution; for a biased product D it must be stated via clause-violation probabilities. (iii) I could not verify the 2^{k/4.82} constant attributed to wangyin2024 (no web access in this run).
findings.fix: Use the 5-approximate decomposition, or the better of it and greedy. State the LLL condition for product D. Double-check the cited constant.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, thm:meta
findings.problem: (i) 'Runs in polynomial time' needs fixed polynomial bounds on DFSB's K and m, and per-module caps. (ii) The output when the intersection is empty (the bad event) is undefined. (iii) DFSB's tightness probability is 1-2delta/M, not 1-delta/M. (iv) Membership in some 'classes above' depends on eps (e.g. Delta <= eps/64 in thm:janson-general). (v) The 'exact' modules must use log-space or exact arithmetic: in doubles, p < 2^-1074 underflows to [0,0], and an intersection with it gives a false verdict p = 0.
findings.fix: Fix the polynomials and caps; output [0,1] on an empty intersection; adjust the confidence accounting; state class membership for a given eps; require overflow-safe arithmetic in exact modules.

findings.location: sec-setting.tex NNF definition (used by all DFSB rules); cor:dfsb(a) "read-once formulas"
findings.problem: (i) 'At most two copies of every gate' fails for large-weight threshold gates; the code makes them opaque nodes (nnf.py), and DFSB's description never says how (F), (D) and (B) treat opaque nodes. (ii) Flattening can create repeated children, e.g. AND(A, AND(A, B)). The code deduplicates them; the paper does not, and without deduplication sv(A) enters Conf and (D) fails. (iii) Read-once formulas containing XOR (allowed by the setting) are not handled exactly: x XOR y becomes the non-decomposable (x AND NOT y) OR (NOT x AND y).
findings.fix: Define opaque nodes and their treatment; add 'deduplicate children after flattening'; write 'read-once {AND, OR, NOT}-formulas'.

referee:ctx-modules:counterexample.verdict: contains false statements. The core results are correct: the Theorem thm:cw construction, F1/F2, decomposability, the d-DNNF claim, cw=0 iff DNNF, Lemma lem:quotient and laminarity inside the output cone. Two statements are false as written, though: (1) because the definition says "nested gates flattened", the Example's cw=O(w) claim fails; (2) the NNF size bound fails under flattening. The module-walk paragraph also claims more than the lemma proves.
referee:ctx-modules:counterexample.checked:
I read sec-setting.tex, sec-envelopes.tex, sec-part1.tex (all of sec:ctxwidth and sec:modules-quotients), thm:sis in sec-part2.tex, the relevant bib entries, code/rareprob/ctxwidth.py, nnf.py, envelope.py, meta.py and families.py. I re-derived F1 and F2, the induction behind M[h,pi] = h|_pi and N[g,sigma] = g|_sigma, the support invariants (supp N[h,.] is contained in sv(h)\kappa(h); supp M[h,pi] in sv(h)\dom pi), decomposability, the per-wire count of (|kappa(h)\dom pi|+1)2^{|kappa(h)|}, determinism, and the multilinear and monotone steps of the lemma. Experiments, all in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-AI-works/02f29707-9759-5ff3-9757-46e1f8b0fdfe/scratchpad:
- t_cw.py: 400 random AND/OR/XOR/NOT circuits with n=1..8, including constants, fan-in-1 gates, repeated children, and marginals q_i in {0,1} or random. Each was compiled with flatten on and off and small_cone 0 and 3, then checked against brute force. Results: phi>0 equals C on every input, the mass equals the brute-force E_D[phi], and the cw=0 iff DNNF test passed in all cases. Where all NNF ORs were semantically disjoint (1350 cases), phi stayed in {0,1}. Edges never exceeded 1.03*(|NNF|+1)(cw+1)2^cw.
- t_big.py: 300 circuits with n=10..19 and cw<=10, sampled inputs: 0 mismatches. XOR/NOT circuits: always a d-DNNF.
- t_flat.py: context width with and without flattening (finding 1, the critical one).
- t_blow.py: quadratic NNF blow-up from flattening (finding 2).
- t_ie.py: the inclusion-exclusion vertex-cover reduction on the Petersen graph with a 4-edge-colouring (#VC = 76 both ways; each colour class is read-once).
- t_quot.py: 3000 random quotients, including thresholds with one-sided perturbations and q in {0,1}. No violation of e^{+-sum xi}; the bound is attained with ratio 1.0.
- t_mod.py: brute-force modules on 300 random circuits. The quotient identity C = Q_g(g, x_rest) held for all 1243 in-cone modules, and laminarity held inside the cone.
The existing pytest ctxwidth tests pass (9/9). Not verified: the Meel-de Colnet venue (SODA 2026, pp. 5978-6010). The web-search budget for this turn was used up, so I could only rely on memory, which recalls the arXiv paper '#CFG and #DNNF admit FPRAS' by Meel and de Colnet. No repository file was modified.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Definition (context width): 'Work in the NNF of C (size <=2|C|, nested gates flattened)'; Example: 'Then cw=O(w), so an FPRAS exists'; same claim in sec-intro.tex lines 72-77
findings.problem: Under the stated definition, flattening merges each window-CNF's AND-tree into a single AND gate. That gate's overlap S_g is every variable occurring in two clauses, so cw = Theta(n/t), not O(w). The Example's claim, and the FPRAS conclusion drawn from it, are false as written. Measured with to_nnf(flatten=True, small_cone=0) on or_of_chain_cnfs(n,3,3): cw = 10, 18, 28, 38 for n = 12, 20, 30, 40. With flatten=False it is 3 each time. A single left-deep window CNF with n=40 also gives cw 38 flattened against 3 unflattened. The code knows this: meta.py, exp_ctx.py and test_ctxwidth_or_of_chains all call to_nnf(flatten=False). The nnf.py docstring says flattening is 'off when the AND-tree shape matters', and families.or_of_chain_cnfs says the left-deep chain 'is what makes the context width small'. So the paper's definition contradicts both the implementation and the experiments, and sec-experiments.tex mentions 'left-deep AND-chains' without the definition allowing them to survive.
findings.fix: Define cw on the unflattened NNF and never merge AND-gates. Merging OR-gates is harmless for cw, since OR-gates contribute no overlap and do not change Up sets; restrict it to fan-out-1 gates to avoid blow-up. In the Example, say that each F_i is bracketed as a left-deep chain of binary ANDs in window order. Then S(acc_k) is the (w-1)-variable overlap of window k with earlier windows, kappa(acc_k) is contained in the window, kappa(c_k) is contained in vars(c_k), and so cw <= w.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Definition (context width) '(size <=2|C|, nested gates flattened)' and Theorem thm:cw 'equivalent to a DNNF of size O(|C| cw 2^cw), computable in the same time'
findings.problem: (a) Flattening shared gates blows the NNF up quadratically. Example: g_1 = x1 AND x2, g_i = g_{i-1} AND x_{i+1}, output = OR of all g_i. Measured NNF wires: 150 to 1375, 300 to 5250, 600 to 20500, 1200 to 81000 for k = 50..400 flattened, against 150..1200 unflattened. (b) sec-setting allows XOR gates and threshold gates with arbitrary weights. The NNF of XOR is O(|C|) but not <= 2|C|. For arbitrary-weight thresholds no NNF expansion is specified: the code makes them opaque 'X' nodes, and compile_ctx returns None. So 'Every circuit C' is neither proved nor implemented. (c) For cw=0 the bound O(|C| cw 2^cw) evaluates to 0. (d) 'Same time' omits the O(|N| n / wordsize) cost of computing supports and contexts.
findings.fix: State thm:cw for circuits over AND, OR, NOT and XOR, plus thresholds handled either by a fixed NNF expansion (e.g. the sequential-counter DP for small integer weights, size O(k*W)) or as frontier gates. Give the bound as O(|N|(cw+1)2^cw), where |N| is the size of the unflattened NNF: at most 2|C| for AND/OR/NOT circuits and O(|C|) with XOR. Running time O(|N|(n + (cw+1)2^cw)). Measured edges never exceeded 1.03*(|N|+1)(cw+1)2^cw.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:ctxwidth intro 'generalises Darwiche's dtree conditioning ... to arbitrary circuits'; sec-intro.tex 'e.g. for ORs of bounded-pathwidth CNFs'; README 'covers, e.g., ORs of bounded-pathwidth CNFs'
findings.problem: cw is a syntactic parameter of the given AND-bracketing and is not invariant under re-association. For the same window CNF (n=40, w=3) cw is 3 as a left-deep chain in window order, 6 balanced, 31 under a random bracketing, and 38 as the standard flat AND of clauses. Darwiche's bound applies to a chosen dtree, normally built from a decomposition. Theorem thm:cw only uses the bracketing it is handed. A bounded-pathwidth CNF given in the usual flat form therefore has huge cw, and the class claim needs a re-bracketing step that is neither in the theorem nor in the code.
findings.fix: Either restrict the claims to CNFs given in path-dtree form, or add a lemma. Lemma: order the clauses by a bag that contains each clause's variables, in a path decomposition of width k, and bracket them as a left-deep chain; then cw <= k+1, since S(acc_k) and kappa(acc_k) lie inside the separator between consecutive bags. Note that such a decomposition is found in linear time for fixed k (Bodlaender-Kloks), while for pathwidth Theta(log n) only approximations exist, giving quasi-polynomial bounds. Optionally define cw* as the minimum over re-associations.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, paragraph after Lemma lem:quotient: 'estimating each module's probability with any sound method ... gives a sound estimator whose relative error is the sum of the modules' errors'
findings.problem: The lemma needs relative accuracy on both q_j and 1-q_j, unless Q is monotone or antitone in y_j. The listed methods (DFSB, Monte Carlo, envelopes, threshold DP) give relative accuracy on Pr[g=1] only. Propagating up the module tree also needs relative accuracy on 1-F, i.e. the lemma applied to NOT Q, which flips the one-sided conditions. Counterexample: C = y AND NOT g2 with g2 an OR of 40 variables, so q2 = 1-2^-40. Monte Carlo estimates q2 to tiny relative error trivially, but 1-q2 is uncontrolled. Numerically, a log-error of 1e-10 on q2 (q2 = 1-1e-10, q2hat = 1-1e-12) changes F = 1-q2 by a factor of 100. Soundness survives if xi_j is computed two-sidedly from the intervals, but the claimed relative error (completeness) does not follow.
findings.fix: Require, for each module, relative accuracy on min(D(g), D(NOT g)), i.e. run the method on the rarer polarity of g, which the NNF has anyway. Then both sides hold within about a factor 2 of xi_j. Alternatively, require each quotient to be monotone or antitone in each module input and estimate the matching polarity; for thresholds and majorities with positive weights the one-sided condition suffices at every level. Say that the module estimates come from intervals valid jointly under a union bound.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:modules-quotients: 'a threshold of 80 random modules with p≈10^{-15} is estimated to 0.1% in seconds'
findings.problem: Nothing in the repository supports this numerical claim. code/rareprob contains no module, dominator or quotient code; grep for 'module|dominator|quotient' finds nothing. No experiment or results file matches it. The closest result, the tilting run in experiments/results/speedup.json (threshold of 400 blocks, p = 2.5e-15), has interval ratio 1.079, about 8%, not 0.1%. Under the paper's own error accounting, 0.1% over 80 sampled modules needs per-module log-accuracy of about 1.25e-5, roughly 10^10/q_j samples each. 'Seconds' is therefore possible only if the module probabilities are computed exactly, e.g. by tabulation, which the text does not say.
findings.fix: Either add an experiment (module detection, exact module probabilities by tabulation, the threshold DP on the quotient) with a table and script, and state that the modules are evaluated exactly, or delete the sentence.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Example: 'counting vertex covers in graphs of degree >=3 is #P-complete'
findings.problem: The wording is wrong and the claim is uncited. The reduction needs bounded maximum degree so that t = Delta+1 = O(1), and the known result is #P-completeness for maximum degree 3 (Greenhill 2000; also Vadhan 2001), not 'degree >= 3'. The (Delta+1)-edge-colouring step also needs a polynomial-time algorithm (Vizing via Misra-Gries). The hard instances (ORs of matching CNFs) have cw=0. They belong to the low-cw class but are not literally sliding-window CNFs. I checked the identity on the Petersen graph with a 4-edge-colouring: #VC = 76 directly and by inclusion-exclusion, and each colour class is read-once.
findings.fix: Write 'graphs of maximum degree 3 [Greenhill 2000]'. State the identity #AND_c phi_c = sum over nonempty S of (-1)^{|S|+1} #OR_{c in S} phi_c, which uses 2^{Delta+1}-1 oracle calls. Cite Misra-Gries for the colouring. Say that hardness holds already in the cw=0 subclass.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Definition of S_g ('a != b children of g') and claim 'cw(C)=0 iff the NNF of C is already a DNNF'
findings.problem: Circuits may have repeated children; the circuit model allows AND(h,h), and the repo's random tests generate them. If children form a multiset and 'a != b' means distinct nodes, S_g misses the self-overlap and the construction emits PROD(M[h,pi], M[h,pi]), which is not decomposable. The iff then depends on an unstated convention. The code avoids this by de-duplicating children in NNF.AND/OR via set(out).
findings.fix: State that NNF gates have de-duplicated child sets (h AND h = h, h OR h = h), or define S_g over pairs of distinct child positions.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:modules-quotients: 'Modules form a laminar family and can be found in O(|C| n) time with dominators, as in fault-tree analysis [dutuitrauzy1996]'
findings.problem: (a) A gate outside the output's cone whose support variables do not reach the output is vacuously a module, and such gates can overlap non-laminarly. Brute force found non-laminar pairs in 20 of 300 random circuits, all among gates outside the cone; inside the cone laminarity always held, consistent with the DAG-ordering argument. (b) Dutuit-Rauzy's algorithm is linear-time and based on DFS visit dates, not dominators. The citation supports a better bound than O(|C| n) by a different method.
findings.fix: Restrict modules to gates in the cone of the output. Write: 'g is a module iff it is an ancestor of every x in sv(g) in the post-dominator tree of the output, so all modules are found in near-linear time; Dutuit-Rauzy give a linear-time DFS algorithm.'

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Theorem thm:cw FPRAS sentence ('rational marginals ... max_i log b_i') and the d-DNNF hypothesis; sec-part2.tex thm:sis(a) on which it relies
findings.problem: b_i is never defined in thm:cw. thm:sis(a)'s 'comparator on ceil(log2 b_i) fresh bits' gives #E' = (prod b_i) D(E) only if the negative literal becomes the range test [a_i <= u_i < b_i]; the test [u_i >= a_i] gives 2^{ceil(log b_i)} - a_i preimages. The identity also needs smoothing with respect to all n variables, otherwise the product runs only over vars(E). The d-DNNF hypothesis 'every OR-gate has semantically disjoint children' must refer to the OR-gates of the NNF in the root's cone, which include De Morgan duals of negated AND-gates. That is much more restrictive than the wording suggests. With these readings the corollary is correct.
findings.fix: Write q_i = a_i/b_i. Specify the literal replacements as x_i -> [u_i < a_i] and NOT x_i -> [a_i <= u_i < b_i], each an O(log b_i)-size OBDD. Smooth over all n variables. Say 'every OR-gate of the NNF (in the root's cone)'.

referee:independence:proof.verdict: needs major fixes. The mathematical core is correct: the first-order sandwich, the full second-order theorem with (H1)-(H6) and the E_3 bound, and the barrier constant 0.29. The problems are around it. The definition of unateness lets XOR and negative-weight threshold gates through, and with those gates the theorem is false as literally stated. The sample size depends on mu, which is never defined and is unknown to the procedure. The Kotecky-Preiss FPRAS claim has no proof (I checked that it is true). Two of the three triangle-freeness numbers in the text do not follow from the stated theorems.
referee:independence:proof.checked:
Every step re-derived by hand, plus exact-enumeration experiments. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-AI-works/02f29707-9759-5ff3-9757-46e1f8b0fdfe/scratchpad (so_check.py, barrier.py, tri.py, tri_small.py, cex.py).

(1) thm:janson-general sandwich:
- p=prod(1-c_i). The bound c_i<=b_i follows from Harris.
- Boppana-Spencer: c_i >= Pr[B_i F_N | F_R] >= b_i - sum_N Pr[B_iB_j|F_R] >= b_i-d_i. Each step is correct: B_i is independent of F_R, and Harris applies to B_iB_j against F_R.
- 1-b+d <= (1-b)e^{d/(1-b)} holds, and sum_i d_i = Delta over unordered pairs.
- Exact enumeration on 1816 random instances found no violation (arbitrary monotone events, q in [0.02,0.95], supports up to 6, up to 7 events).

(2) The procedure's thresholds:
- With b_hat_i <= 1/3, and rejection when max b > 1/2, the factor Delta/(1-max b) is at most 2 Delta.
- The Delta thresholds eps/64, eps/16 and eps/4 are consistent.
- If |log M_hat - log M| <= eps/4 and p is in [M, M e^{eps/2}], the interval [M_hat e^{-eps/4}, M_hat e^{3eps/4}] contains p.
- The variance of log M_hat is sum b_i/((1-b_i)N) <= 2mu/N, and the quadratic remainder is O(mu/N) once b_hat <= 1/3.
- The stated cost is a valid (loose) upper bound.

(3) thm:second-order:
- I re-derived the formula for c_i in terms of nu, and each of (H1)-(H6), including that the events in R'' are independent of B_i and B_j and that Pr[F_R] <= Pr[F_{R''}].
- Both Bonferroni directions, both cases C_i >= Theta'_i and C_i < Theta'_i (using C_i >= 0 and X >= 0 from Harris), and both halves of the E_3 derivation are correct. No errors found.

(4) prop:pairwise-barrier:
- I enumerated p_stars and p_triangles directly; the difference is q^3(1-q).
- The minimum of log(1+q^3(1-q)/(1-3q^2+2q^3))/(3q^3) is 0.29391 at q=0.2790, so 0.29 is correct; it also holds on all of (0,1).
- The dependency graphs and the pairwise data match.

(5) Mobius expansion and interface DP:
- mu(T)=0 for any T that is disconnected in G.
- The interface-DP identity is correct, and interval arithmetic is sound because the expression is a polynomial with nonnegative coefficients.
- The Kotecky-Preiss condition b <= (2e^3 d)^{-r} is sufficient. I derived it by bounding cluster weights with Finner's inequality.

(6) Triangle-freeness example: I checked my counting formulas by brute force at N=11 for three different event orders, then evaluated them at N=10^4.

(7) Bibliography entries for Boppana-Spencer 1989, Kotecky-Preiss 1986, Mousset-Noever-Panagiotou-Samotij 2020 and Harris 1960 are correct, and the description of what MNPS proves is accurate.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:independence, definition 'Call C unate if there is a sign pattern such that every path from x_v to the output has the same parity of negations ... checked syntactically'; used as the hypothesis of thm:janson-general
findings.problem: The Setting (sec-setting.tex) allows XOR gates and threshold gates [sum w_j y_j >= t] with arbitrary weights. The parity of NOT gates along a path certifies nothing through such gates: x XOR y, or [-x >= 0] (which is NOT x), has no negation on any path. Under the literal definition, both the sandwich and the procedure's soundness fail. Concrete counterexample, all variables uniform: A_1 = x OR y, A_2 = [-x>=0] OR y'. No path contains a NOT gate, so C is 'unate' by the definition. Then b_1 = b_2 = 1/4, D(B_1B_2) = 0 so Delta = 0, M = 9/16, but p = 1/2 < M. The procedure passes both pre-tests (b_hat <= 1/3 with high probability, and Delta_hat = 0 always) and outputs an interval around 9/16 of log-width eps, which misses p whenever eps < 0.47. With M' disjoint copies, log(M/p) = 0.118 M'.
findings.fix: Define unateness on the NNF: every input variable occurs in literals of only one polarity. Equivalently, compute path parities in a circuit where XOR gates make their inputs binate and threshold gates with negative weights count as negations. Say explicitly that this is the check run in O(|C| n) time.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, thm:janson-general, 'estimate every b_i with O((mu+1)eps^{-2}) independent samples' and the proof's 'N=O((mu+1)/eps^2)'
findings.problem: mu is never defined in this subsection; elsewhere in sec-part1 mu denotes a pilot hit count. Presumably mu = sum_i b_i. It is unknown to the procedure, yet soundness on every circuit needs N >= c mu/eps^2. With smaller N, the standard deviation of log M_hat, about sqrt(mu/N), exceeds eps/4, and the median trick does not help because each repetition fails with probability above 1/2. Simulation with m=10^4 independent events, b_i=0.1, eps=0.1 (so mu=1000): N=100/eps^2 gives |log M_hat - log M| > eps/4 in 92% of runs. As written, the procedure's soundness depends on an unspecified choice of N.
findings.fix: Define mu = sum_i b_i. Make N computable: either use mu <= m (N = O((m+1)/eps^2)), or take an upper confidence bound from the pre-test samples. With N_0 >= 10 ln(1/delta) samples per event and mu_hat_0 = sum b_hat_i, Bernstein (independent summands bounded by 1/N_0, variance <= mu/N_0) gives mu <= max(2 mu_hat_0, 10 ln(1/delta)/N_0) with probability 1-delta. Then use N = C(2 mu_hat_0 + 1)/eps^2 with C about 100; my simulation shows that N = 4 mu/eps^2 still fails 62% of the time. Also state that the b_hat_i entering M_hat are the gated ones (b_hat_i <= 1/3), so the Taylor remainder bound applies.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, 'Beyond pairs' (ii): 'a Kotecky--Preiss argument certifies the tail when max_i b_i <= (2e^3 d)^{-r} ..., giving an FPRAS for bounded d'
findings.problem: An FPRAS with a specific constant is asserted with no proof. The non-obvious ingredient is missing. Without monotonicity, the cluster weights |w(gamma)| = Pr[intersection over gamma of B_i] cannot be bounded through correlation inequalities; the exponent r needs Finner's generalized Hoelder inequality, which gives Pr[intersection over gamma of B_i] <= prod_{i in gamma} b_i^{1/r} when every variable lies in at most r events. The precision issue is also not addressed: each mu(T) is an alternating sum of 2^{|T|} logarithms of estimated probabilities. 'd the degree' and 'r the number of events per variable' should say maximum. I checked the claim and it is true.
findings.fix:
Add a proof sketch:
- Write the polymer representation Pr[AND A_i] = sum over compatible families of connected gamma of prod w(gamma), with w(gamma) = (-1)^{|gamma|} Pr[intersection over gamma of B_i], where polymers are compatible when they are disjoint and non-adjacent in G. Then mu(T) is the sum of the clusters whose support is exactly T.
- Bound |w(gamma)| <= beta^{|gamma|} with beta = (max b)^{1/r}, by Finner.
- Apply Kotecky-Preiss with a(gamma) = |gamma| and decay g(gamma) = |gamma|. A connected set of size s containing a given vertex is one of at most (ed)^{s-1}, so the per-vertex sum is at most sum_s (ed)^{s-1}(e^2 beta)^s <= 2^{-s}/(ed) summed, i.e. <= 1/(ed), when beta <= 1/(2e^3 d). Multiplying by (d+1)|gamma| gives (2/e)|gamma| < a(gamma).
- Hence the tail over clusters of size >= s is at most m e^{-s}; truncate at s = ln(m/eps).
- There are m(ed)^s = poly(m/eps) connected sets T of size <= s for bounded d. Each needs the probabilities Pr[AND_{U subset of T} A_i] to additive accuracy eps/(m(2ed)^s), which costs poly(m/eps) samples.
- Alternatively, downgrade the sentence to a remark without the FPRAS claim.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, after thm:janson-general: 'triangle-freeness of G(N,q) at N=10^4, mu=10, the window is e^{+-0.023}'; Second order paragraph: 'the first-order window is e^{2.1} while the second-order one is e^{+-0.055}'
findings.problem:
These numbers do not follow from the paper's theorems, and they mix conventions. With mu = C(N,3) q^3, the unordered Delta = C(N,2)C(N-2,2) q^5, as used in thm:janson-general, is 0.0230 at mu=10 and 1.067 at mu=100.
- At mu=10 the window ratio is e^{0.023}, i.e. e^{+-0.0115} about the geometric mean, not e^{+-0.023}.
- At mu=100 it is e^{1.07}, not e^{2.1}; 2.13 is the ordered-pair Delta.
- For E_3: sum_i Theta'_i is order-independent and equals the sum over connected triples, (7/12) N^5 q^7 + N^4 q^6/6 = 0.01831. Theta_i and beta_i C_i contribute about 1e-5 each, and (1-beta)(1-b) is about 1. So E_3 = 0.0183, the window is e^{+-0.018}, and the actual sandwich ratio is about e^{0.018}. The text says +-0.055, three times larger. (I checked the counting formulas by brute force at N=11 for three orders.)
- No script in experiments/ reproduces any of these numbers.
- Related: thm:janson defines Delta over ordered pairs with a factor 1/2, while thm:janson-general uses unordered pairs; the same symbol has two meanings.
findings.fix: Replace with 'window e^{0.023}' at mu=10, and with 'first-order window e^{1.07}, second-order e^{+-0.018}' at mu=100. Use one Delta convention throughout (unordered pairs, as in thm:janson-general, and restate thm:janson as e^{Delta/(1-eps_0)}). Add the script that computes these numbers to experiments/.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, thm:janson-general, output interval [M_hat e^{-eps/4}, M_hat e^{3eps/4}] and 'It is complete when ...'
findings.problem: The output interval has ratio U/L = e^{eps} > 1+eps, so it is not 'tight' in the sense of def:sound (U <= (1+eps)L). The completeness claim is therefore off by a constant in eps.
findings.fix: Run the procedure with eps' = ln(1+eps), which is at least eps/2 for eps <= 1: output [M_hat e^{-eps'/4}, M_hat e^{3eps'/4}] with Delta thresholds eps'/16 and eps'/64. Alternatively, state completeness as U <= e^{eps} L.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, thm:janson-general, 'estimate Delta by sampling dependent pairs' and the cost bound
findings.problem: The Delta estimator and its error analysis are not given, so the claimed pre-test guarantees (reject when Delta > eps/4, accept when Delta <= eps/64) and the |E(G)| eps^{-1} cost term are unsupported. Estimating each pair separately with Hoeffding at confidence delta/|E| would need far more samples. 'Evaluations' with a sum_i |A_i| factor is really gate-operation count.
findings.fix:
Specify the estimator: estimate each D(B_iB_j), (i,j) in E(G), from N_Delta = ceil(C eps^{-1} ln(3/delta)) fresh samples, and set Delta_hat = sum of the estimates. Its variance is <= Delta/N_Delta and its summands are bounded by 1/N_Delta, so Bernstein gives:
- if Delta <= eps/64, P(Delta_hat > eps/16) <= exp(-9 N_Delta eps/256);
- if Delta > eps/4, P(Delta_hat <= eps/16) <= exp(-9 N_Delta eps/128).
The pre-test b_hat_i <= 1/3 needs O(log(m/delta)) samples per event, with a union bound. The cost is sum_i |A_i| deg_G(i) N_Delta, which is at most the stated bound. Say 'gate evaluations' or 'time'.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:independence, 'after flipping the negative variables, every B_i is increasing'
findings.problem: Orientation slip. Flipping the variables whose paths have odd parity makes C, and hence every A_i (the top AND-tree has no negations), increasing, so every B_i = NOT A_i becomes decreasing, not increasing. Harris needs only a common direction, so nothing breaks, but the sentence is literally wrong.
findings.fix: Write 'after flipping the variables that occur positively (or: after a global flip), every B_i is increasing'. Alternatively, note that Harris applies to any family of events that are all monotone in the same direction.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Second order paragraph ('gives |log p - log M_2| <= E_3') versus appendix.tex thm:second-order
findings.problem: The main text omits the hypothesis beta_i = sum_{j in N_i} b_j < 1, which the appendix assumes. It also does not say that E_3 carries the denominators (1-beta_i)(1-b_i), so 'a sum of third-order quantities' is only accurate when every beta_i is bounded away from 1.
findings.fix: Add 'when every beta_i = sum_{j<i, j~i} b_j < 1', and write E_3 = sum_i (Theta_i + Theta'_i + beta_i C_i)/((1-beta_i)(1-b_i)), or refer to it explicitly.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, 'Beyond pairs' (i), interface dynamic programming

referee:cftp:proof.verdict: needs major fixes. The proofs in sec:cftp hold up: Prop. prop:truncation, the anti-monotonicity and Häggström–Nelander exactness claim, the bias accounting and the gamma coalescence bound are all correct. But Thm. thm:cftp is missing a hypothesis: every event must have b_i ≤ 1/2, and for general unate circuits b_i must also be certified. Without it the staging step "Harris-guaranteed r_k ≥ 1/2" can fail. telescoping_estimate in code/rareprob/cftp.py does not check this hypothesis, and on valid unate CNFs it returns intervals that miss p far more often than delta allows. referee:cftp:proof.checked:
Paper (sec-part1.tex, subsection sec:cftp, plus sec:independence for the unateness definition and Harris):
(1) Prop. prop:truncation is correct. pi = (1-theta) pi_T + theta pi_{>T} gives d_TV(pi_T, pi) = theta * d_TV(pi_T, pi_{>T}) ≤ theta. The Chernoff step is also right: if theta > eta then X ~ Bin(R, theta) has mean mu > eta R and the threshold eta R/2 ≤ mu/2, so Pr[X ≤ eta R/2] ≤ exp(-mu/8) ≤ exp(-eta R/8) ≤ delta.
(2) The heat-bath update on D|F, with F a down-set, is x_v <- [u<q_v] AND [x^{v->1} in F]. This is the exact heat-bath conditional for states in F, and it is decreasing in x_{-v} on all of {0,1}^n, so the chain is anti-monotone in the HN sense. The cross-over bounding chain (L_v = f(u, U), U_v = f(u, L)) keeps L ≤ X ≤ U for every chain started in F. It also preserves interval inclusion, so coalescence from -T implies coalescence from -2T at the same value, and CFTP with doubling and reused randomness is valid. Coalescence happens almost surely whenever D(F) > 0, by a positive-probability sweep, so the sampler is Las Vegas.
(3) Bias in Thm. thm:cftp is correct: |r'_k - r_k| ≤ theta_k, relative shift ≤ 2 eta when r_k ≥ 1/2, and (1 + eps/(8m))^m ≤ e^{eps/8} ≤ 1 + eps/4.
(4) The coalescence bound is correct, including for general increasing events. A site can newly disagree only if u < q_v and some event containing v has a disagreeing co-member. That gives E|D_{t+1}| ≤ (1 - gamma/n)|D_t| with gamma = 1 - q_max r (k_max - 1), so Pr[no coalescence by T] ≤ n e^{-gamma T/n} and T = O((n/gamma) log(nm/eps)). Simulation on the 2x10 ladder confirms the bound holds (it is conservative).
(5) Variance by product of independent ratio estimates and Chebyshev plus median: correct given r'_k ≥ 1/2 - eta.
(6) Citations hn1998 and pw1996 are correctly attributed and cited.

Code (cftp.py):
(1) CFTP mechanics are correct. Randomness for times -1..-T is reused when T doubles, and new randomness is appended for the older times. The L/U updates use each other's old values. Padding columns n (always 1) and n+1 (always 0) handle short and absent clauses, and unit clauses fire correctly.
(2) The sampler matches the target: on a 2x3 hard-core ladder with 200k samples, TV to the exact D|F is 0.003, which is noise level.
(3) Truncation TV ≤ failure fraction holds empirically at several T_max settings.
(4) The repetition count is right: _reps_for(0.025) = 13 with binomial tail 0.0243, and Chebyshev with eps0 = 2 sqrt(v) gives ≤ 1/4 per repetition conditional on the halted counts.
(5) The union bound is right: delta/2 for the median plus K x delta/(2K) for the KL truncation certificates.
(6) Relative variance ≤ 1.5/n_k per stage when r' ≥ 0.4.
(7) The upper end hi = med e^b/(1-eps0) is valid.
(8) The lower end lo = med/((1+eps0)e^b) is valid, but only by an argument the docstring does not give (see findings).
(9) The Harris clamp is deductive.
(10) Coverage in the valid regime is fine: 30/30 runs contain p on a 14-variable 2-CNF.

findings.problem: stages() always opens a new stage with the next clause, even when 1 - D(B_c) < 1/2. Such a clause becomes a singleton stage whose guaranteed ratio is only 1 - D(B_c) < 1/2. But the variance bound 1.5/n_k and the bias factor th/(0.5 - th) both assume r_k ≥ 1/2, so the returned interval is invalid. The input is a legitimate unate CNF and is_unate accepts it. Reproduction: 10 unit clauses [(i,1)] with q_i = 0.02, so p = 1.02e-17 and every stage ratio is 0.02. With N=200, hi < p in 16 of 20 runs; with the default N=2000, hi < p in 5 of 20 runs. Nominal delta is 0.05 (exp1.py, exp1b.py).
findings.fix: Use a per-stage Harris guarantee h_k = prod_{c in stage k}(1 - pb_c) instead of the constant 1/2. Require th_k < h_k, otherwise return no verdict. Set the bias term to a_k = th_k/(h_k - th_k). Set the variance bound to v = prod_k (1 + (1 - h_k + th_k)/((h_k - th_k) n_k)) - 1. Alternatively, return 'no verdict' whenever max_c pb_c > 1/2.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Theorem thm:cftp ('group the events into stages with Harris-guaranteed ratios r_k ≥ 1/2 ... for every unate circuit')
findings.problem: The staging step needs every b_i ≤ 1/2: an event with b_i > 1/2 cannot be placed in any stage with guaranteed ratio ≥ 1/2. The bias argument (relative shift 2 eta) and the variance argument both rely on r_k ≥ 1/2, and nothing in the statement guarantees it. The coalescence condition gamma > 0 does not imply it either. For unit clauses k_max = 1, so gamma = 1 for any q. For a perfect matching with q = 0.9, gamma = 1 - 0.9 > 0 but b = 0.81. Second gap: for general unate circuits, as opposed to unate CNFs, b_i = D(not A_i) is not computable. Staging on point estimates can produce a stage whose true Harris product is below 1/2. The proof sketch and the code only treat CNFs, where b_i is a product of marginals.
findings.fix: Add the hypothesis max_i b_i ≤ 1/2, or state the general version. With per-stage guarantee rho_k = prod_{i in stage}(1 - b_i), the relative shift is eta/rho_k, the per-stage relative variance is ≤ (1 - rho_k + eta)/((rho_k - eta)N), and one needs eta ≤ eps rho_min/(16m). For general unate circuits, first estimate each b_i additively, e.g. to ±0.05 with O(log(m/delta)) samples each, union-bounded over the m events. Then stage using the upper confidence bounds b_i^+ and charge their failure probability to delta.

findings.location: code/rareprob/cftp.py, UnateSystem.__init__ (line 51-52: self.vars, self.pb = prod r[i] for i in vars)
findings.problem: If a clause repeats a variable, pb multiplies r_v once per occurrence. is_unate accepts this, since the sign is consistent. So D(B_c) is underestimated: r_v^2 instead of r_v. The Harris clamp lo = max(lo, prod(1 - pb)) then exceeds p, and the stage guarantees are wrong too. Reproduction: clauses [(0,0),(0,0)] and [(1,0),(1,0),(2,0)] with q = 0.5. Then p = 0.375, but the code returns lo = 0.656 and hi = 0.419, an empty interval that excludes p (exp7.py). janson_interval in janson.py computes P(B_i) the same way and probably has the same issue.
findings.fix: Deduplicate the variables of each clause before computing vars and pb, e.g. self.vars = [sorted({i for i, _ in c}) for c in clauses], and compute pb from the deduplicated lists. Do the same in janson.py. Alternatively, reject clauses with repeated variables.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Theorem thm:cftp: 'estimate each r_k with O((mu+1)/eps^2) truncated exact samples'
findings.problem: mu is never defined. It appears undefined in thm:janson-general too, and from context it is the expected number of violated events, sum_i b_i. The proof sketch also never links the number of stages K to mu, yet that link is what makes N = O(K/eps^2) equal O((mu+1)/eps^2).
findings.fix: Define mu = sum_i b_i. Add: with b_i ≤ 1/2, greedy staging closes a stage only when the stage plus the next event has sum of -ln(1 - b) > ln 2. Summing, K < 1 + 2 sum_i(-ln(1 - b_i))/ln 2 ≤ 1 + 4 mu, using -ln(1 - b) ≤ 2 ln2 b on [0, 1/2]. Hence N = O(K/eps^2) = O((mu+1)/eps^2) samples per stage and O((mu+1)^2 log(1/delta)/eps^2) in total.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, Theorem thm:cftp: 'certify each stage's truncation at level eta = eps/(16m) by prop:truncation' and 'The output is within (1±eps)p with probability 1-delta'
findings.problem: The delta bookkeeping is missing: each of the m certificates must run at level delta/(2m), which requires R = ceil(8 ln(2m/delta)/eta) = O(m log(m/delta)/eps) runs per stage. That certification cost is not stated, and when m >> mu/eps it dominates the O((mu+1)/eps^2) estimation budget. It is also wasteful to use m where the number of stages K ≤ 4mu + 1 suffices. Two smaller points. First, 'within (1±eps)p' only holds when the output is not 'fail'; under def:sound the output should be the interval [p_hat/(1+eps), p_hat/(1-eps)]. Second, the completeness claim needs Pr[tau > T] well below eta for the threshold test to pass with probability 1 - delta. Example: with theta ≤ eta/16, Pr[X > eta R/2] ≤ (e/8)^{eta R/2} ≤ (delta/m)^{4}. This is where T ≥ (n/gamma) ln(256 n m/eps) comes from.
findings.fix: State eta = eps/(16K), certify at level delta/(2K) with R = ceil(8 ln(2K/delta)/eta) runs per stage, and give the total cost: O(K^2 log(K/delta)/eps + K(mu+1) log(1/delta)/eps^2) CFTP runs, each of at most T = O((n/gamma) log(nm/eps)) updates. Rephrase the conclusion as a sound interval, or 'fail'.

findings.location: sec-part1.tex, sec:cftp paragraph before thm:cftp: 'is then an exact Las Vegas sampler for D|F_{<k}, whatever the events are'
findings.problem: The claim is correct, but two hypotheses are left implicit, and the almost-sure termination that 'Las Vegas' requires is not argued. 'Anti-monotone' holds in the Häggström–Nelander site-wise sense (Pr[x_v=1 | x_{-v}] is decreasing in x_{-v}), not for the update map as a whole. The events must be increasing, which is what makes F a down-set. CFTP halts almost surely only if D(F_{<k}) > 0.
findings.fix: Add: 'for increasing events B_i with D(F_{<k}) > 0 (guaranteed by Harris when all b_i < 1)'. Add a one-line termination argument. With positive probability within a window of n steps, every site with q_v < 1 is updated with u ≥ q_v, and then every site with q_v = 1 is updated. After that window L = U, because 1_{q=1} lies in F when D(F) > 0. Disjoint windows are independent, so coalescence happens almost surely.

So the syntactic test as worded does not guarantee that the B_i are increasing, and the Harris and anti-monotone arguments in thm:cftp need them to be.
findings.fix: Define unateness on the NNF instead, with ⊕ expanded and thresholds rewritten: each input variable occurs as a literal of only one polarity. Equivalently, count a negative-weight threshold input as a negation and treat ⊕ inputs as occurring with both polarities.
